# Project: Build a universal AI chat-to-local-agent handover tool that extracts structured context from chat interfaces and generates agent-specific output artifacts for any supported local coding agent.
<!-- Generated by handover v1.0.1 from claude chat on 2026-04-08T03:29:02.462278Z -->

## Tech Stack
- Language: Python
- Framework: CLI (with browser extension)
- Database: none

## Key Decisions
- Use structured handoff artifact files (TASK.md, PLAN.md, CLAUDE.md, etc.) plus a local HTTP bridge server rather than a universal cross-platform protocol (rationale: No vendor-neutral universal handoff protocol exists today; artifact-driven handoff solves the real pain point immediately without waiting for vendor agreement)
- Implement agent-specific file generation as an incremental feature on top of the existing BaseTarget adapter architecture, not a major rewrite (rationale: The repo already has a pluggable target registry, BaseTarget abstraction, and per-agent adapters; this fits cleanly as a feature extension)
- MCP server is planned for a later phase (v1.0.0 roadmap Phase 6), not the current core (rationale: Current priority is stabilizing the browser extension and local bridge server; MCP adds universality later on top of a working artifact-first foundation)
- Use shared semantic extraction with target-specific artifact generation: each target adapter declares its own filenames and rendering logic (rationale: Keeps the parser/summarizer pipeline reusable while letting each agent target emit the files it actually needs)
- Perform a full codebase review first, then do targeted feature-level reviews on each subsequent PR or branch (rationale: Establishes a baseline health assessment before iterating on individual features)

## Constraints
- Do not redesign the parser/summarizer pipeline
- Do not break existing Claude Code target behavior
- Do not add speculative complexity without clear payoff
- Keep Python 3.11 compatibility
- Maintain 80% test coverage gate
- Do not overclaim unsupported functionality in docs or extension UX
- Backward compatibility for existing CLI flags and workflows must be preserved

## Non-Goals
- Implementing a fully realized universal agent-to-agent protocol platform in the current phase
- Adding large new features like a VS Code extension
- Replacing or redesigning existing targets
- Adding cloud or service integrations
- Overengineering the target model with heavy frameworks

## Open Questions
- [ ] What are the official or product-canonical output filenames for Codex and Copilot targets — are SPEC.md and TASKS.md the right conventions or should the repo define its own?
- [ ] Should the browser extension version be kept separate from the Python package version, and if so how should that be communicated clearly in docs?
- [ ] Is a lightweight artifact-spec abstraction (each target declares a list of named artifacts with filenames and templates) worth introducing now, or should targets continue to own rendering directly?
